title: 3. Strict Schemas
use_cases: Implement when frontend components require structured JSON objects to prevent application crashes
Configure when industry-standard formatting like Fountain Markdown syntax is mandatory
Use when trading execution speed for high-level deterministic control is acceptable
Apply when building multi-phase LLM pipelines rather than single-prompt architectures
Use when automatic error recovery for malformed model responses is required
content:
When you are building a UI, you can’t rely on vibes. You need structure. If the AI returns a markdown block when your frontend expects an object, your app crashes.

We force JSON output for everything, even the creative writing parts.

- Retry Logic: If Gemini returns malformed JSON or forgets to fill in a value, our API automatically catches the error and retries the request.
- Formatting Cheat Sheets: We don’t hope Gemini remembers Fountain Markdown screenwriting syntax; we inject a “cheat sheet” directly into the prompt to ensure compliance.
- Screenwriting Conventions: We enforce rigid schemas for character naming conventions (e.g., distinguishing between a “First Introduction” and a “Dialogue Cue”) to ensure the output is industry-standard.

This approach turns the “fuzzy” logic of an LLM into the deterministic logic your app needs.

I’m not going to lie to you: building this system wasn’t all sunshine and perfect prose. When you move from “one big prompt” to a “5-phase pipeline,” you are trading simplicity for control. And that trade comes with a price tag.

Here are the reality checks you need to consider before you start coding.
